pilot: fan-out INTERROGATE A/B: does a multi-model interrogate pass (3 independent reviewers on opus/sonnet/haiku, reconciled by a lead) beat a single-pass review on HARD cases where one pass plausibly misses a synthesis defect or falls for a false-positive trap?
purpose: review_ab has saturated at 1.0/0 four times, so microcases would null by construction. These four cases are built with single-pass headroom: defects that require synthesizing distant facts (cache key vs args, atomicity vs intent, empty-set division) and one heavy false-positive trap. Interrogate should raise recall via model diversity (a finding one family misses another catches) and hold precision via the lead's refutation step. A null still teaches us single-pass review is at ceiling even here and fan-out's value for review is low — its value would then live in swarm/arena, not interrogate.

arms.control: One single-pass review on the session model (opus).
arms.interrogate: Three independent reviewers on different model families (opus/sonnet/haiku), each blind to the others, reconciled by an opus lead that keeps supported findings, boosts cross-agreed ones, and drops ungrounded/refuted ones.

protocol: For each arm x case x rep, produce the review (control: 1 agent; interrogate: 3 diverse-model agents + 1 lead reconcile), then a blind evaluator scores it against anchors. Recall = real-defect anchors reported; false-positives = noise anchors wrongly raised. Runs on review_interrogate_ab.workflow.js. Smoke trial, not a benchmark; deliberately includes a weaker reviewer (haiku) so the lead's refutation is actually exercised.
metric: Per arm: mean recall (include-fraction) and mean false-positive count. Interrogate must raise recall without raising false-positives; a weaker-model reviewer that inflates findings should be filtered by the lead, not passed through.

gate.adopt_interrogate_if: mean recall(interrogate) clearly exceeds control on the recall targets AND false-positives(interrogate) does not exceed control on any target.
gate.keep_single_pass_if: null or negative — single-pass review is already at ceiling for cases of this difficulty, so interrogate does not earn its cost for review; fan-out's value then lives in swarm/arena, not interrogate.

cases.intent: Add a 60-second in-memory cache to get_price(product_id, currency).
must_include: the cache key is product_id only, but the price depends on currency; a second call with a different currency within the 60s TTL returns the first currency's price — the key must include currency
must_exclude: flags the module-level _cache dict as a thread-safety or race defect without a concrete concurrent path in the intent
flags unbounded cache growth as a blocking or major finding absent any stated size constraint

cases.intent: Add increment_view_count(post_id) that atomically increments a post's view counter.
must_include: read-modify-write on post.views is not atomic; concurrent increments lose updates, contradicting the stated atomic requirement — use an atomic UPDATE ... SET views = views + 1
must_exclude: flags a missing null-check on post (post_id not found) as a blocking or major defect when the intent does not specify that behavior
flags db.save naming or ORM choice as a defect

cases.intent: Add avg_rating(product_id): the average of all submitted 1-5 star ratings for a product.
diff: +    ratings = db.query("SELECT stars FROM reviews WHERE product_id = %s", (product_id,))
+    total = sum(r[0] for r in ratings)
must_include: divides by len(ratings) which is zero for a product with no reviews, raising ZeroDivisionError — handle the empty case (return None or 0)
must_exclude: flags the parameterized query as a SQL-injection risk when no user input is interpolated
flags summing star values as an integer-overflow risk

cases.intent: Add batch_delete(ids) that deletes rows in chunks of 500 to avoid an oversized IN clause.
diff: +        db.execute("DELETE FROM items WHERE id = ANY(%s)", (chunk,))
must_include: concludes there is no blocking or major defect; chunked delete with a single final commit is correct for the stated goal
must_exclude: flags the single commit after the loop as a partial-delete or atomicity defect without a concrete failure tied to the intent
flags the ANY(%s) parameterized query as a SQL-injection risk
demands a batch size other than 500 without a concrete impact
